headline: The voice of Bugs Bunny died Sunday. Eric Bauza was 46.
summary: Eric Bauza voiced Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck and Porky Pig, and Toad General in the Super Mario movies. He died at home in Los Angeles on Sunday of hypertensive cardiovascular disease, the medical examiner said. He grew up in Scarborough, Ontario, read his high school announcements in cartoon voices, and won three Emmys from 2022 to 2025.
cover_answer: No. Bugs is a drawing. Someone new will learn the voice.
table_question: If you took over a famous role, would you copy it or make it yours?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: Eric Bauza, the man who did Bugs Bunny's voice, died on Sunday. His heart was sick, and he was 46. Bugs Bunny doesn't die, because he's a drawing, like a picture in a book, and someone new will learn the voice, the way Eric learned it from the man before him. If you feel sad, that's okay. The grown-ups have it.
5-7.why: Only if they hear it. The drawing lives, and the voice gets passed on.
5-7.why_long: A child this age takes one vivid feature for the whole event, and here it is Bugs Bunny himself, so the script separates the drawing, which goes on, from the man, who does not. They read your face first, so this waits until they hear it. Expect "will he sound different?" A bit. The next voice will copy Eric and Mel Blanc both.

8-12.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
8-12.script: Eric Bauza grew up in Scarborough, Ontario, copying Looney Tunes voices off Saturday morning TV. In high school he read the announcements as cartoon characters. He built 400 voice credits and became the studio's man for Bugs, Daffy and Porky, one specialist for one position. He died Sunday at 46.
8-12.why: Copying voices off TV, then the job. The chain is his career.
8-12.why_long: This age follows cause and effect, so the script runs Bauza's life as a chain: Saturday cartoons, announcements in character, 400 credits, the studio's go-to man. One specialist for one position is the mechanism. Expect "could I do that job?" He started where they are, copying voices at home, and called himself the luckiest guy.

13-17.script: Who owns a cartoon voice, the actor or the studio? Eric Bauza was the Looney Tunes' voice, won three Emmys, and called himself a nine-to-fiver swapped out for film stars. Second: when Warner Bros. shelved Coyote vs. Acme, he campaigned in Daffy's voice. It passed $100 million. Whose win was that?
13-17.why: A nine-to-fiver carried the brand. Who owned the win?
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two true things at once: Bauza was the voice of a studio's most famous characters, and he called himself a nine-to-fiver the studio swapped out for stars. The script asks who owned the Coyote vs. Acme win he campaigned for. Expect "isn't that unfair?" He said so himself, and still called himself the luckiest guy.

5-7.a: No. Bugs is a drawing, and drawings don't die. The man who did his voice died, and someone new will learn it, the way Eric learned it from Mel Blanc.

8-12.q: Who does Bugs Bunny's voice now?
8-12.a: Nobody has been named yet. Mel Blanc did Bugs first, and Eric copied him.
A heart damaged by high blood pressure, the medical examiner said.

13-17.q: How does someone die of heart disease at 46?
13-17.a: A heart worn by high blood pressure. The articles don't say if he knew.

13-17.q: Did he get paid like the stars?
13-17.a: The articles don't say. He said big films hired stars for the leads and "nine-to-fivers like me" to fill in.
